h1: AC Repair in Uptown / Galleria, Houston
title: AC Repair Uptown / Galleria, Houston | AC Repair Houston
description: High-rise and mixed-use towers where the cooling is rooftop chillers and shared systems, and condo interiors where the indoor unit sits in a closet.
intro: Cooling in this part of Houston is mostly not a single-family condenser sitting in a side yard. Much of it is rooftop equipment, chillers and shared systems that serve an entire tower, and the work is a different discipline from a residential call. Inside the units, the fan coil often lives in a closet off the hallway, which sets its own limits on access and on what can be changed.
localAngle: This is a high-rise and mixed commercial and residential district, so the equipment is shared. Rooftop units, chillers and cooling towers serve whole stacks of floors rather than one household, and a fault in that equipment shows up as several tenants complaining at once instead of one house being warm. Condo interiors add a second problem: the indoor coil and fan coil are usually behind a closet door in a finished hallway, where access is narrow and every duct connection is in a space that was never sized to be opened up.
commonCalls: Several units on different floors of the same tower reporting the same problem at once
A rooftop unit that trips or will not restart after a storm
A fan coil in a hallway closet dripping into the corridor or onto the floor
Tenant spaces that swing from cold to warm depending on when the chillers run
Condensate lines on a tower that drain slowly because the pan has scaled up

faqs.q: My whole floor is hot but the rest of the building is fine. What is likely wrong?
faqs.a: In a tower with shared plant, the fault is usually in the branch that serves that floor, not the whole system. That could be a zone valve that has failed shut, a duct connection that has separated, or a fan coil that has tripped its own breaker. The building's maintenance records and the tenant improvement drawings for that floor will tell the technician where to start.

faqs.q: How is rooftop equipment different from a house condenser?
faqs.a: A rooftop unit or chiller handles a far larger load, sits on a roof that bakes all afternoon, and feeds a network of ducts and chilled water lines rather than one set of registers. A residential condenser is a single machine with a coil and a fan. The service access, the safety requirements and the diagnostic instruments are different, and the technician who works on them needs the ones that match.

faqs.q: The indoor unit is behind a closet door. Can it still be repaired?
faqs.a: In most cases yes, but access is what drives the work. A fan coil in a finished hallway closet often sits in a space barely wider than the unit, with the drain line and the coil already boxed in. The technician will need to know the closet dimensions and how the unit was installed before quoting anything, because getting a replacement into a tight closet is sometimes the whole job.

faqs.q: Who should I call about a chiller problem in a building?
faqs.a: For equipment serving more than one unit, the building or property manager normally handles it, since the chiller, the cooling tower and the rooftop units are building systems. If you are the manager or owner, request commercial service and give the technician the equipment tag, the fault history and the recent service logs. If you are a tenant, the property manager is the right first call, because they control access to the mechanical spaces.

faqs.q: Is a service call in a tower more expensive than the same call in a house?
faqs.a: It can be, and the reason is usually not the fault. A single fault in one fan coil is a small job, but a fault in a shared piece of plant affects the whole stack, and that work pulls in the access equipment, the hours the building can be down, and a technician who knows the system rather than the unit. The towers around Greenway Plaza and Uptown Grove have different mechanical layouts for the same reason, so a one-off call into a building whose records the technician cannot see is a slower visit. Ask who is paying for the visit and what the visit covers before it is booked, because a tenant calling about a building fault and a manager calling about the same fault are two different conversations.

faqs.q: Why did the whole building get warm during the heat wave when my unit was running?
faqs.a: That points at the plant rather than at your fan coil. The chillers and the cooling tower serving a stack like Chase Tower are sized for the floors and the retail space attached to them, and on the hottest afternoon of the year the plant can hit its limit while every unit in it is still running normally. The cooling tower is part of that story: it rejects heat into the same wet air the building is sitting in, so the water running through it comes back warmer than it should. A fault that shows up across many floors at once and clears on a cooler evening is a plant fault. We send the request to a company that already works Uptown and Galleria, and that company can read the loop temperatures and the tower condition to tell you which side of that line it is on.
